label: verify-bm-polyamide-sls

claims.claim: PA12 (PA2200) water absorption 0.52 wt% at 23C/50%RH, 1.33 at 96%RH, 1.93 in 100C water
claims.source_says: Water absorption % 1.93 | ISO 62 / DIN 53495 % 1.33 | Water absorption % 0.52 (pdftotext rows; labels and conditions in separate columns)
claims.note: The three values are in the datasheet; the column layout is garbled, so I could not read each condition label beside its value, and I took the order from the agent's mapping.

claims.claim: 5.5-10.5 wt% immersion uptake of sintered PA12 is mostly void water (density 0.90-0.95 vs 1.01 dense); dense PA12 saturates at 1.6%
claims.source_says: UZH PA2200 datasheet: Density 0,90 – 0,95 g/cm3. Springer page would not open (paywall/redirect); Crossref gave only the title 'Effect of water absorption on the properties of selective laser-sintered PA12 specimens'.
claims.note: The sintered density is confirmed, but I could not open the Springer text for the 10.49% and porosity wording or the 1.6% dense value, and the void-versus-swelling conclusion is the agent's own inference.

claims.claim: PA11 bulk water diffusivity at 23C is 4.95e-13 m2/s; PA12 same order; 0.8 mm strip needs 76-126 h to 90% equilibrium, 4x with one face sealed
claims.note: The PA11 D value matches, but the paper has no PA12 data; the PA12 range and the 76-126 h time come from the agent's own calc, which I did not rerun.

claims.claim: No measured hygroscopic expansion coefficient exists for PA11/PA12/TPU; vendor gives 0.2% dimensional change at 1.4% uptake for PA12, giving free strain 0.1-0.2% and bilayer R of 130-1000 mm
claims.source_says: PowerCore, with a maximum absorption of 1.4%, has a corresponding dimensional change of 0.2%.
claims.note: The vendor figure is real, but it is for cast PA12GC fully submerged, not laser-sintered PA12. The 'no measured coefficient exists' claim, the 0.1-0.2% strain over 30-80% RH and the bilayer radius are unsourced extrapolation.

overall: One claim is supported and three are partly supported. The datasheet numbers, the PA11 diffusivity and the vendor 0.2% at 1.4% figure are real. The Springer paper would not open, so the 10.49% void-water and 1.6% dense-PA12 figures are unchecked. The PA12 diffusivity range, the equilibration times and the bilayer radii are the agent's own derivations. The 1.4% vendor figure is for cast PA12, not sintered.
